story.why: When studying graph algorithms and sorting mechanisms for competitive programming, dry pseudo-code in textbooks made it hard to develop intuition for edge-case traversals.
story.problem: Static textbook diagrams fail to show how pointers mutate state in real time, especially during recursive calls, tree rebalancing, and heapify passes.
story.how_solved: Engineered a frame-by-frame execution engine in JavaScript that serializes data structure states, tracks memory swap operations, and renders step-by-step playback with speed controls.
story.challenges: Handling pause/resume states across deep recursive tree traversals without blocking the UI thread or exceeding browser call stack limits. Solved using async generator functions that yield execution state step-by-step.
story.learned: Visual intuition turns hard algorithmic concepts into second nature. Also learned the immense power of JavaScript generator functions for stateful animations.
story.improvements: Add support for custom graph input via interactive drag-and-drop nodes and integrate real-time Big-O asymptotic curve overlays.

title: StudySync
tagline: Real-time Collaborative Focus Rooms & Resource Vault

story.why: Built during the 48-hour HackCode Global Sprint. Remote study groups during exam seasons suffered from fragmented tools—jumping between video calls, shared docs, and timers.
story.problem: Students lost 20+ minutes per session coordinating materials, synchronization of focus blocks, and shared note links across 4 different platforms.
story.how_solved: Architected a unified Flask application featuring synchronized room clocks, pinned resource boards, markdown notes, and minimal distraction interfaces.
story.challenges: Synchronizing timer states across different device latency offsets during a 48-hour sprint. Implemented a server-authoritative timestamp calculation to eliminate client clock drift.
story.learned: How to rapidly scope an MVP under tight time pressure, communicate effectively with teammates, and write resilient backend error middleware.
story.improvements: Replace SSE polling with WebSockets and introduce persistent voice channels using WebRTC.

title: DevLog Engine
tagline: Terminal-first Developer Journal with Git Commit Correlation

story.why: I wanted an frictionless way to document what I learned every day directly from my terminal without breaking flow state or opening heavy note apps.
story.problem: Context switching to browser apps caused distraction, and notes were rarely tagged with the exact git commits where lessons actually occurred.
story.how_solved: Built a fast command-line utility in Python that inspects local git repositories, captures the latest commit message and diff, and appends structured markdown journal entries.
story.challenges: Cross-platform terminal path resolution and handling detached HEAD git states gracefully without crashing the CLI prompt.
story.learned: UNIX philosophy: write programs that do one thing well and compose with standard stdin/stdout streams.
story.improvements: Package as a pip distribution on PyPI and add automated weekly digest generation.

story.why: Traditional habit trackers are rigid and track simplistic boolean checkboxes. I wanted to quantify actual coding hours, difficulty tiers of solved problems, and language shifts.
story.problem: Lack of visual feedback made it hard to see macro progress over months, causing occasional bouts of imposter syndrome.
story.how_solved: Designed a responsive client-side dashboard with interactive Chart.js visualizations that ingest JSON-exported coding logs and render multi-axis growth trends.
story.challenges: Ensuring responsive canvas chart resizing without blurry high-DPI scaling artifacts on mobile screens and maintaining smooth 60fps animations.
story.learned: Device pixel ratios in canvas rendering, data normalization principles, and color contrast accessibility for complex charts.
story.improvements: Direct integration with GitHub GraphQL API and LeetCode profile scraper for automated daily synchronization.

title: Markdown Knowledge Vault
tagline: Lightweight Self-hosted Wiki with Bidirectional Links

story.why: Frustrated by proprietary note-taking tools locking personal thoughts behind paywalls and binary formats, I wanted a local-first plain text system.
story.problem: Linking concepts across multiple technical domains (e.g. databases, algorithms, operating systems) required bidirectional [[wiki-links]] that standard markdown viewers lack.
story.how_solved: Built a Flask web app that scans local markdown files, indexes header tags and [[bracketed]] references into an SQLite inverted index, and renders an interactive relationship graph.
story.challenges: Building a custom regex parser that handles nested code blocks and escape sequences without false-positive link matches.
story.learned: Relational graph indexing, SQLite full-text search extensions, and template caching strategies.
story.improvements: Add an interactive force-directed canvas graph using D3.js to navigate the note constellation visually.

story.why: My very first multi-component frontend project after finishing DOM manipulation fundamentals. I wanted a timer that respected browser privacy with zero tracking.
story.problem: Most web timers are bloated with ads, require accounts, or lose state if you accidentally reload the tab.
story.how_solved: Crafted an ultra-clean, dark glassmorphic web app with browser Web Workers for accurate background interval tracking and Web Audio API synthesized chimes.
story.challenges: Browser tab throttling when inactive caused setInterval to drift. Solved by shifting interval tracking into a dedicated Web Worker thread.
story.learned: Browser background execution constraints, thread separation in modern web browsers, and synthesized audio frequencies.
story.improvements: Add keyboard shortcuts (Space to toggle, R to reset, S to skip) and ambient brown noise generator.
